title: Fruit of the Fungi
about: KC and Kristi Mangine run Fruit of the Fungi as a family farm in the town of Lebanon, in the hills of Madison County, about an hour southeast of Syracuse. In 2005 they bought a home and 47 acres in the hamlet of Lebanon Center, land first homesteaded in 1840. By 2008 they were growing shiitake on logs and selling them seasonally to restaurants and farmers markets. In 2015 the farm went full time and year-round.

Today the Mangines grow certified organic shiitake, lion’s mane, oyster, maitake, beech, chestnut and reishi mushrooms. Every variety grows on wood, the way these mushrooms grow in a forest, using sawdust recycled from local mills as the growing medium. The farm controls that substrate from start to finish. They concentrate on fresh and dried mushrooms for the table rather than kits or supplements.
Since the winter of 2016 they have been regulars at the CNY Regional Market. You can find them year-round at the Saturday farmers market in the C shed, a few miles from Eden.
